claim: Hearthhull does nothing until another creature taps to station it, so have a creature in play the turn before you cast it. Horizon Explorer adds only 2 counters. The Beast tokens from Baloth Prime add 4 each, and Baloth Prime itself adds 10. Cast Baloth Prime and sacrifice a land the same turn to start the Beasts coming, then get Hearthhull to 8 counters (flying, vigilance, haste) as fast as you can.
evidence: Game 1: only Horizon Explorer was stationing, so Hearthhull sat at 2 and then 4 counters from rounds 4 to 5 and never attacked. Game 2, round 4: Baloth Prime came down and Escape Tunnel was sacrificed for a 4/4 Beast. In round 5 a Beast put Hearthhull straight to 4. In round 6 a second Beast took it to 8, and Hearthhull, Broodship and Explorer attacked for 12. In round 8 Baloth Prime alone stationed it to 10.

Game 0041, round 6 (table turn 23): the pilot cast Hearthhull and Safekeeper, then sacrificed a Forest to Safekeeper. Szarel's trigger made Tireless Provisioner 5 power. Tapping Provisioner (5), Szarel (2) and Safekeeper (1) gave exactly 8 counters. Without the Szarel counters it would have had only 6. Hearthhull then attacked for 6 that turn.

Game 0051: on round 3 the pilot cast Scute Swarm, then played and cracked Escape Tunnel for two Insects. On round 4 Myriad Landscape added a third, and it cast Hearthhull and stationed it to 4 with the Swarm and three Insects. Mazirek took it to 6 on round 5 and a freshly cast Brushrazer took it to 8 on round 6. It attacked for 6 with haste that same turn.

claim: After Hearthhull is recast, tap two 4-power Beasts to station it: it goes straight back to 8 counters and has haste, so the drain and draw work that same turn. Removal on Hearthhull costs you only the commander tax, as long as you keep two untapped 4-power creatures for it.
evidence: Game 2, round 9: The Kami War had exiled Hearthhull. It was recast for 8, two Beasts put it to 8 counters, and it sacrificed Stomping Ground at once for the drain that took Terra from 1 to -1.

claim: Save Rakdos Charm's graveyard-exile mode for effects that bring back a whole graveyard, such as a saga or spell that returns all lands. Do not spend it stopping one flashback or one reanimation target. It is also the deck's cheap instant answer to an artifact, so keep it for either job.
evidence: Game 2, round 5 (turn 19): it answered Summon: Titan's chapter II and exiled 12 cards from Terra's graveyard, 7 of them lands with four fetchlands among them, before they could come back. Game 1, round 3 (turn 11): the Charm only stopped Kuja's Flashback on a single Dark Ritual. Nothing was left to answer Kuja's artifacts or board later, and Kuja won.

Game 0051: Rakdos Charm was held open from round 6 on against Wilhelt's Zombie Apocalypse. On round 10 Planetary Annihilation killed four Zombies (22 power), and Wilhelt had no mana left to return Relentless Dead. Rakdos Charm then exiled Wilhelt's 12-card graveyard, including Zombie Apocalypse, Gravecrawler and the dead Zombies.

claim: Do not aim Putrefy or other destroy removal at a creature whose indestructibility depends on something the opponent can change at instant speed. Ozai, the Phoenix King is indestructible at 6+ unspent mana, and its controller can tap a land in response to reach 6. Use exile instead (Tear Asunder kicked), or cast destroy only when they cannot reach the threshold even by tapping everything.
evidence: Game 2, round 7 (turn 25): Putrefy targeted Ozai while Zuko had 5 unspent mana. Zuko tapped a Mountain in response, reached 6, Ozai became indestructible and the Putrefy was wasted.

claim: Once Hearthhull has 8 charge counters, Sylvan Safekeeper (and Zuran Orb) are free sacrifice outlets. Each land you sacrifice to them makes every opponent lose 2, at no mana cost and even at instant speed. Before you tap lands for spells, count your lands times 2 against each opponent's life. The whole mana base can be a lethal drain.
evidence: Game 0041, round 7 (table turn 26): Hearthhull was at 8 counters. The pilot sacrificed five lands to Sylvan Safekeeper's shroud ability, with no mana spent. That was 10 life from each opponent: The Wise Mothman at 7 and Fire Lord Zuko at 9 both died, and it won the game.

claim: Aim Putrefy at an opponent's counter-stacked commander on your own main phase, when its controller is tapped out and before they can give it ward or protection. Holding Putrefy open for several rounds is fine, but fire it once one creature threatens a commander-damage kill.
evidence: Game 0041, round 5 (table turn 19): Tidus, Yuna's Guardian was 13/13 with 10 counters, had already dealt Zuko 16 commander damage, and Innkeeper's Talent could reach level 2 (ward). Putrefy killed Tidus while its controller had no mana open, and the counters were lost when it went to the command zone. Tidus had to recast it from zero.

claim: When Hearthhull is destroyed or dies, move it to the command zone right away, at the moment it hits the graveyard. If you leave it there, you cannot cast it again without a recursion card. Recasting it for {2} more and restationing it with untapped creatures is the whole plan after removal.
evidence: Game 0051, round 6 (table turn 23): Feed the Swarm destroyed Hearthhull at 8 counters, and Wilhelt even told the pilot it could go to the command zone. The pilot left it in the graveyard. Its notes on rounds 7, 9 and 10 say 'Hearthhull is stuck in the graveyard, so I can't cast it again from the command zone' and 'no recursion yet'. The deck played its last five rounds without its commander, while Rampaging Baloths, a Beast token and Augur of Autumn were in play and could have restationed it.

claim: Mazirek, Evendo Brushrazer and Hearthhull's drain trigger only on sacrifices. A creature destroyed by a wrath, by removal or by lethal damage does not count. Do not put their triggers on the stack for deaths that were not sacrifices, and do not count on them against a destroy-based sweeper. Grave Pact, Fleshbag Marauder and your own land sacrifices do count.
evidence: Game 0051, round 5 (table turn 19): the pilot put two Mazirek triggers on the stack when Zombie Apocalypse destroyed Ozai and Generous Plunderer. The auditor ruled them illegal. On table turn 22, Brushrazer was destroyed by Chandra's Ignition damage and correctly did not trigger.

claim: Keep Worldsoul's Rage until X can kill a player outright. Its X also brings back up to X lands from your graveyard, so the same spell rebuilds your mana base after land sacrifices.
evidence: Game 0051: on round 8 the pilot held Rage with Obeka at 11. On round 9, with Obeka at 5, it cast X=5 from 7 lands. That knocked Obeka out and returned Eumidian Hatchery, Festering Thicket and Escape Tunnel, taking the pilot from 7 lands to 10.
